 “The saddest match of my career”: Cobolli fights back tears after his Turin exit 
 After a 7-6(6), 6-0 defeat on his ATP Finals debut in Turin, the world No 6 tried to hold back his tears when asked about his season, then spoke of pride, sacrifices, a crowd he felt he let down and a dream he wanted to enjoy.
 18 November 2026 
 Cédric Rouquette 
 Reporting from Turin 
 Flavio Cobolli, ATP Finals 2026 | © FITP 
 Anyone who has spent time around Flavio Cobolli knows the Italian is all in: generous, wholehearted, fully committed to his tennis dream. By far the defining image of these ATP Finals so far, his fight to hold back the tears in his press conference after losing to Frances Tiafoe , 7-6(6), 6-0 on Wednesday night, felt like the logical consequence of the evening.
 “This is definitely the match that makes me the saddest of my career,” the Italian said quietly.
 The world No 6, a Roland-Garros finalist this year, is out of the ATP Finals in Turin on his debut, at home, without winning a set. The question that brought him close to tears was not about the match but about his season. He asked for it to be repeated, seemingly to buy time. After a long silence, Nicola Arzani, the ATP’s head of communications, brought him tissues. Cobolli laughed, then went to the roots of the emotion.
 Because what he spoke about first, in Italian, was pride. “That is certainly something that makes me proud. I think nobody in this room thought I could make it to the Masters, nobody in my team either, and not even me. So it makes me happy. I know I have a lot of room for improvement, and that makes me even happier.”
 But there was no room for happiness on Wednesday: “Today I can’t be happy.” His result, and the one-way traffic of the second set, let too many people down. “Playing in Italy is always difficult for us, but it is also a big dream.”
 I’m also a bit sorry for the crowd, who always supported me.
 That crowd had given him an ovation at 0-5 in the second set, when he appeared on the big screen, dejected by the score, by his level, by the inevitable. “So I’m very disappointed, but at the same time I’m proud of the season, of the people I found by my side. It’s a result built on a lot of sacrifices. Other players deserve to be here.”

 But once again, the match did not live up to that story. “I’m trying to cultivate this dream with a lot of fun, and today, in the second set, I didn’t have fun. I felt a lot of weight on my shoulders.” Not a question of tension or pressure, he insisted, almost in denial. “I just wanted to do well for the crowd and for the people who work with me, and today I didn’t.”
 Alcaraz on Friday, then the Davis Cup
 Cobolli has not forgotten he still has a match to play, against Carlos Alcaraz , who has already qualified as winner of the Lendl Group. It is a dead rubber for the standings, but not for him: “It’s a beautiful gift. I hope to annoy him as much as possible, even if it won’t be easy.”
 His year will not quite end there, though. He said his participation on Friday and in the Davis Cup is “not at risk”. Italy’s Final 8 takes place in Bologna from 24 to 29 November.
